headings.title: SMTO-EXE-0190 — SMTO has nowhere to save or find this PDF

html:
SMTO-EXE-0190 — SMTO has nowhere to save or find this PDF

GUID: 6208b872-34af-5083-a333-e8bfb42dd9c8
Slug: pdf-artifact-failure
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: pdf

What happened

  • PDF results are normally saved with the task's Artifacts, but this step ran without a task area to use and wasn't told a folder to save to, or it pointed to a saved file it couldn't reach from here. Nothing was saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Chat and ask SMTO for the PDF step in a conversation. A conversation gives the step a place to keep its results in the task's Artifacts list.
  2. Or give SMTO a full folder path and a new file name ending in .pdf on the computer that runs the Gateway. With a clear destination, SMTO can save a single PDF without a task area.
  3. If the step makes several PDFs, such as splitting a file, run it from a conversation rather than giving one file name. One file name can hold only one PDF, so several results need the task's Artifacts list.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the new PDF it created, and it appears in the task's Artifacts list or in the folder you named.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with where you started the request (Chat, a Workflow or a Schedule), to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A PDF operation had no current run artifact directory: an artifact-workspace:// input could not be resolved, or output publication had neither a conversation/run artifact scope nor an explicit output_path.

What this means

  • PDF input resolution lacks the requested artifact-workspace root, or output publication has neither an owning artifact scope nor an explicit supported output path. PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.

Why this can happen

  • PDF input resolution lacks the requested artifact-workspace root, or output publication has neither an owning artifact scope nor an explicit supported output path.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect run/conversation scope and whether the request uses an artifact URI or a single explicit output file.

How to fix it

  • Dispatch the PDF operation with conversation_id and run_id so the Gateway can resolve OF_RUN_ARTIFACT_DIR, or pass an explicit create-only output_path for operations that produce exactly one PDF. artifact-workspace:// inputs resolve only inside the current run's artifact directory.
  • Run with an active conversation/run artifact scope, or provide an explicit create-only output_path for a single PDF.

Retry and execution caution

  • Run with an active conversation/run artifact scope, or provide an explicit create-only output_path for a single PDF.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended artifact resolves within its owning run, or a valid new single-output destination is supplied.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
